summary: Fourteen days of good-quality CGM data (98.7% coverage) show overall time-in-range of 86.0% with elevated variability (CV 32.6%), time-below-range of 5.1% (above common targets), and time-above-range of 8.9%. Documented level-2 hypoglycemia clustered on 2026-08-13, 2026-08-14, and 2026-08-21, and level-2 hyperglycemia clustered on 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-18. No carbohydrate or e-carb entries exist anywhere in the package; all 655 insulin entries are automated correction boluses or temp basal, so meal-bolus, carb-ratio, and e-carb behavior could not be empirically validated. Afternoon hours (roughly 13:00-17:00 local) show the day's worst hyperglycemia, overlapping repeated user-initiated 135 mg/dL temporary targets that structurally blunt SMB delivery, while overnight hours (00:00-03:00 local) show elevated lows despite the day's lowest basal rate, suggesting a delayed tail effect from evening corrections and long duration of insulin action rather than an overnight basal excess. These patterns have multiple plausible, overlapping explanations that current data cannot fully separate; no profile or automation parameter change is strongly supported yet, and priority is placed on safety review and targeted observation before adjusting any single setting.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage 98.7% (3995/4046 expected), 5-minute cadence, 10 gaps (largest 65 min), no duplicates or invalid entries. Day 2026-08-07 is a partial day (33 readings) and down-weighted in trend interpretation. Zero carbohydrate entries exist anywhere; all 655 insulin entries are correction boluses or temp basal, with COB=0 in every sampled loop status. A mid-period Profile Switch on 2026-08-13 to a 'u200 dilute basal - FLAT ISF' profile is noted as context only, per instructions not used to infer historical inapplicability of the currently declared authoritative profile.

analysis_steps.findings: Aggregate TIR 86.0%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1%, CV 32.6%. Level-2 lows (<54 mg/dL) documented 2026-08-13 (17:00-17:15, down to 42), 2026-08-14 (18:04-18:15, down to 41), and 2026-08-21 06:19 (42). Level-2 highs (>250 mg/dL) documented 2026-08-15 (~16:30-16:40) and 2026-08-18 (~11:54-12:14). Local-hour pattern shows overnight (00:00-03:00) TBR elevated (10-18%) despite the day's lowest basal segment, and afternoon (13:00-17:00) shows the worst TAR, peaking 32.1% at hour 16, followed by a rebound TBR spike at hour 19. A pump Occlusion/Pump Error announcement occurred 2026-08-19, flagging that day's data for cautious interpretation.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight (00:00-03:00 local) hypoglycemia elevation occurs during the day's lowest basal rate (0.6 U/h), arguing against overnight basal excess as primary driver; more likely a delayed tail effect from evening correction dosing combined with a tight 90 mg/dL overnight target. Sparse overnight loop-status samples (2 points) show 'no temp required' at those instants, weakly supporting this. Afternoon hyperglycemia (peaking local hour 16) coincides with the day's lowest basal step (0.5 U/h at 16:00), but this is confounded by repeated user-initiated 135 mg/dL temporary targets during the same window and by the total absence of carb logging, so no isolated basal defect can be confirmed.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.basal_segments; hourly_glucose_local hours 0-3,9-17; representative_events Temporary Target entries; representative_loop_statuses 2026-08-11T00:11, 2026-08-16T00:00.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carb data to separate meal vs basal effect; only 7 basal segments vs. hourly glucose granularity; very small overnight loop-status sample.

analysis_steps.findings: ISF is a single flat 56 mg/dL/U segment, but Dynamic ISF (enabled, 70% adjustment factor) produces wide effective sensitivity swings across loop statuses (roughly 28-179 mg/dL/U-equivalent) that move in the expected direction (stronger at highs, weaker at lows); directional logic appears sound, magnitude adequacy unresolved. Carb ratios cannot be validated at all because zero carb entries exist. DIA of 10 hours is unusually long and, combined with a custom 'free_peak_oref' insulin model lacking a documented peak-time parameter, cannot be fully assessed; it is a plausible but unconfirmed contributor to the overnight tail-effect hypothesis. Frequent SMB stacking (3-minute interval) confounds single-bolus therapy_response_windows, making aggregate/hourly patterns more reliable than individual bolus-response windows.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.isf_segments, carb_ratio_segments, dia_hours; smb_settings.raw_settings (dynamic_sensitivity_enabled, dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent, insulin_type); representative_loop_statuses variable_sens values; therapy_response_windows 2026-08-14T16:20 example; representative_treatments stacked boluses.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carb entries anywhere (CR fully unvalidated); no peak-time parameter for the insulin model; SMB stacking confounds single-window response analysis; only 2 overnight loop-status samples.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are enabled and functionally necessary given that 100% of bolus-type treatments are corrections with zero carb entries; UAM is not duplicating COB counting since COB is always 0. smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled=false combined with repeated user-initiated 135 mg/dL temporary targets on 2026-08-09, -17, -18, -19, -20 means SMB delivery is likely restricted during those windows; two of these windows (2026-08-17, 2026-08-18) overlap the days with the highest observed TAR, a plausible partial explanation for afternoon highs alongside unlogged-meal and basal-timing hypotheses. A single well-documented instance on 2026-08-14 shows a severe low (41-48 mg/dL) followed about 25 minutes later by a loop status showing rapid rebound to a high with near-maximum basal engaged, consistent with an undocumented rescue-carb rebound met by aggressive automated correction, though this is one instance, not a confirmed recurring cycle.
analysis_steps.evidence: treatment_summary; representative_events Temporary Target entries; hourly_glucose_local hours 13-17; glucose_extremes 2026-08-14 cluster; representative_loop_statuses 2026-08-13T13:55, 2026-08-14T18:40; smb_settings.raw_settings.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No per-event visibility into SMB gating decisions during temp-target windows; no carb or rescue-treatment log to confirm the 2026-08-14 rebound hypothesis directly; only one documented instance of the hypo-to-rebound cycle.

analysis_steps.findings: max_basal_u_per_hour (12 U/h) and max_iob_units (25 U) are far above observed usage (peak IOB 5.935 U, peak enacted basal about 4 U/h), so these explicit caps are not the binding constraint; the lower current_basal_safety_multiplier appears to be the effective limiter, and this is not flagged as needing change. autosens_enabled=false alongside dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true is an internally consistent deliberate configuration, not a broken state; sensitivity_ratio values of 1 and near 1 across samples are neutral readings, not evidence Autosens is disabled and inert. 'Dosing sensitivity' values swing more than four-fold across samples (about 40 to 179), a plausible but unconfirmed contributor to the overall CV of 32.6%, confounded with SMB interval/strength settings and temporary-target timing. Carb-absorption settings (min_5m_carbimpact, meal_max_absorption_hours) are never exercised in this dataset since COB is always 0, so they remain entirely untested rather than validated.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_settings.raw_settings; representative_loop_statuses sensitivity_ratio and dosing-sensitivity values across multiple dates; glucose_summary.coefficient_of_variation_percent.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No visibility into the custom algorithm branch tokens seen in reason strings, limiting confidence that stock oref1/Dynamic-ISF documentation fully explains observed swings; no carb ground truth to separate competing explanations; sparse loop-status sampling (24 entries over 14 days).

analysis_steps.findings: The user-declared analysis_context.meal_strategies array is empty and strategy_stable_for_period is null, so no declared prebolus, immediate-bolus-percentage, or e-carb values exist to reproduce; this is a genuine absence in the declared source, separate from the telemetry-confirmed absence of carbs. Telemetry confirms zero carb-linked boluses; all insulin delivery is reactive correction/UAM or temp basal. This confirms in form (not in content) the hypothesis that observed hyperglycemia is met reactively rather than anticipated via a prebolus or carb-ratio calculation. A recurring dosing-intensity pattern independent of meals is also visible: several corrections given at already-high glucose are followed by large delayed drops by 120-360 minutes (2026-08-13T13:05, 2026-08-15T02:30, 2026-08-19T15:55), suggesting IOB-stacking dynamics rather than a meal-timing issue.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate or meal-timestamp data of any kind exists to assess bolus timing relative to a meal.

analysis_steps.findings: extended_carb_entries=0 and average_extended_carb_duration_min is null; no therapy_response_window has is_extended_carbs=true. E-carbs are not used anywhere in the period, so no e-carb amount, start offset, or duration can be assessed, and no e-carb-versus-pump-extended-bolus comparison is possible. The carbohydrate absorption model settings (min_5m_carbimpact, meal_max_absorption_hours) remain entirely untested since COB is always 0.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No e-carb or regular-carb entry exists to observe an absorption or action-time curve against.

analysis_steps.findings: Combining all stages, no single profile or automation parameter change is isolatable from confounds: overnight lows are best explained by a correction/IOB tail effect interacting with a tight overnight target and long DIA rather than basal excess; afternoon highs have at least three overlapping plausible explanations (unlogged meals, SMB suppression during self-set 135 mg/dL temporary targets, and the 16:00 basal step-down) that current data cannot separate; and meal/CR/e-carb settings cannot be evaluated at all due to zero carbohydrate logging. The single highest-value next action is establishing meal-linked evidence (even approximate carb logging) before altering CR, prebolus, or e-carb settings, while the highest safety-relevant action is understanding the recurring correction-at-high-glucose-then-large-delayed-drop pattern and the temporary-target/SMB interaction before any profile or automation number is changed. Sequential, single-variable verification is recommended throughout.
analysis_steps.evidence: All prior stage findings and evidence combined; decision_inventory review; profile_context.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate logging; sparse loop-status sampling; unresolved confounds between meal timing, temporary targets, and basal timing for the afternoon pattern; single-instance evidence for the hypo-to-rebound cycle.

strengths: CGM data coverage is good (98.7%) with consistent 5-minute cadence and no duplicate or invalid entries, giving a reliable basis for the patterns identified.

Several overnight hours (04:00-08:00 local) show strong time-in-range (95-99%) with low variability, indicating that base overnight-into-morning control works well outside the identified tail-effect window.

Dynamic ISF sensitivity ratios move in the clinically expected direction across sampled loop statuses (stronger correction at highs, weaker at lows), indicating the automated sensitivity layer is functioning as designed rather than erratically.
issues: Documented level-2 hypoglycemia clusters on 2026-08-13, 2026-08-14, and 2026-08-21, and level-2 hyperglycemia clusters on 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-18, with overall time-below-range (5.1%) above common targets and elevated glycemic variability (CV 32.6%).

Recurring afternoon hyperglycemia (local hours 13-17, peaking 32.1% time-above-range at hour 16) overlaps repeated user-initiated 135 mg/dL temporary targets that structurally restrict SMB delivery, a plausible partial contributor alongside unlogged meals and basal timing.

A recurring dosing pattern of correction boluses given at already-high glucose followed by large delayed drops 120-360 minutes later (2026-08-13, 2026-08-15, 2026-08-19) suggests possible IOB-stacking dynamics that warrant closer review before any dosing-strength setting is changed.
Complete absence of carbohydrate and e-carb logging prevents any evaluation of carb ratios, prebolus timing, immediate-bolus percentage, or e-carb behavior.

recommendations.title: Review recurring hypoglycemia clusters and the correction-then-delayed-drop dosing pattern with a clinician before any other change
recommendations.description: Level-2 lows on 2026-08-13, 2026-08-14, and 2026-08-21, plus a repeating pattern of large glucose drops 2-6 hours after high-glucose corrections, suggest an IOB-stacking or tail-effect dynamic that should be understood before adjusting basal, target, DIA, or SMB strength, since changing any of these together would make the cause unidentifiable.

recommendations.title: Clarify the purpose of repeated 135 mg/dL temporary targets before considering smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep the current target segments (90 mg/dL overnight and 23:00, 100 mg/dL daytime) unchanged for now, since the overnight hypoglycemia pattern appears more consistent with a delayed tail effect from evening correction dosing and the long duration of insulin action than with the target itself, and the basal rate is already at its daily minimum during the affected hours.

Changing the target without first confirming whether the driver is IOB tail, DIA, or SMB timing would make the true cause unidentifiable, and the instructions caution against altering dependent insulin-delivery settings together.

education: Time-below-range above about 4% and a coefficient of variation above 36% are commonly used thresholds of concern in glucose management guidelines; this dataset's CV of 32.6% and TBR of 5.1% are close to or above these reference points and warrant attention.

Dynamic ISF and Autosens are two different ways of automatically adjusting insulin sensitivity; having Autosens disabled while Dynamic ISF is enabled is a deliberate alternative approach, not a partially broken configuration.
A sensitivity_ratio value of 1 in a loop status means no adjustment was applied at that moment, not that the adjustment mechanism itself is turned off.

Insulin-on-board (IOB) from a correction bolus can remain active for the full duration of insulin action (DIA); with a 10-hour DIA, insulin from an evening correction can still be lowering glucose well past midnight, which can look like an overnight basal problem when it is actually a lingering bolus effect.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only; TuneMyBG prepares data for review and does not provide medical advice.
Every proposed change in this analysis must be independently verified by the user and discussed with a qualified clinician or care team before being applied.
Changes to insulin delivery settings should be made one at a time, with close glucose monitoring afterward, to allow the effect of each change to be identified separately.
Do not change AAPS settings automatically based on this analysis; all changes described here are review suggestions only, not directives.
